mainTopic: Hair grows from the root, the נזיר shaved by bandits (רבי אליעזר's seven-day rule), and which methods of removing hair make a נזיר liable
overview: The גמרא finishes a proof that hair grows from the root: people who dye their hair get undyed roots. It then challenges this with a ברייתא. A נזיר shaved by bandits who still has enough hair to bend its tip to its root does not lose his days. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a shaving after his term was finished, and it follows רבי אליעזר, who says that anything after the term costs only seven days. רבי אליעזר learns this by comparing the end-of-term shaving to the shaving after טומאה. Since hair grows a bend-to-root length in seven days, the hair left on him already covers what is needed. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that a נזיר is liable for removing hair in any way. רבי יאשיה learns this from 'קדוש יהיה גדל פרע'. רבי יונתן says only a razor brings punishment, and he reads that phrase as adding an עשה to razor shaving. Another ברייתא learns the wide rule from 'לא יעבור על ראשו' and explains that the word 'razor' teaches that the final shaving must be done with a razor. Its explanation of why this cannot be learned from a מצורע continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof finished: hair grows from the root
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the people who dye their hair ends: their roots show undyed hair, so hair grows from the bottom. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the roots of their hair the new hair is undyed. Learn from this that hair grows from the bottom. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof from the end of the previous amud: people who dye their hair get undyed hair at the roots. So hair must grow from the bottom, and the גמרא agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If hair grew from the tip, the dyed part would stay near the scalp and new hair would show at the ends. Since the undyed hair shows at the roots, the new growth must come from below. The repeated שמע מינה shows that the גמרא accepts the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: roots, the bottom part (here, of the hair)
their hair
learn from it / we can conclude
it grows from underneath

phrases.english: at the roots of their hair (the new hair is undyed).
Learn from it that hair grows from the bottom.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a proof begun on the previous daf.
steps.raayaObject: That hair grows from the root.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that people who dye their hair get undyed roots.

steps.title: Challenge from the נזיר shaved by bandits
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a נזיר shaved by bandits does not lose his days if enough hair is left to bend its tip to its root. If hair grows from the bottom, he should lose them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about this ברייתא: a נזיר whom bandits shaved, leaving enough hair to bend its tip to its root, does not lose his days. If you think hair grows from the bottom, he should lose them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the conclusion it just reached by bringing a ברייתא that seems to fit badly with the idea that hair grows from the bottom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If hair grows from the bottom, the short hair left near the scalp is only the newest growth. The hair that grew during his time as a נזיר was cut away. So the ברייתא's ruling that he loses nothing looks hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: bandits, robbers
to bend its tip to its root (a short, set length of hair)
cancels the days already counted, so he must count them again
and if you were to think

steps.confusionAlert: סותר here does not mean the נזיר's whole status is cancelled. It means he loses the days he already counted and must count them again.

phrases.english: But what about this that is taught in a ברייתא:
a נזיר whom bandits shaved,

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁיְּירוּ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לָכוֹף רֹאשׁוֹ לְעִיקָּרוֹ —
phrases.english: and they left him enough hair to bend its tip to its root —
he does not lose his days.
And if you think hair grows from the bottom,
let him lose his days!

steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that hair grows from the bottom.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If hair grows from the bottom, the remaining hair is only new growth and the hair of his time as a נזיר is gone, so he should lose his days. Yet the ברייתא says he does not.

steps.title: The shaving happened after the term was finished, following רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a shaving after his term was finished. It follows רבי אליעזר, who says anything after the term is complete costs only seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where they shaved him after his term was completed. Whose view is this? רבי אליעזר's, who says: anything after the completion costs only seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The bandits shaved him after his term was over but before he brought his קרבנות, and the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that once the term is complete, a problem costs only seven days, not the usual thirty for shaving. That shrinks how much hair growth we need to worry about to just seven days. The next steps explain why that matters.

keyTerms.meaning: after the term was completed
and whose view is it?

phrases.english: It is a case where they shaved him after the completion of his term.
phrases.notes: He means after the days were counted but before he brought his קרבנות.

phrases.english: And whose view is it? It is רבי אליעזר,
who says: anything after the completion
cancels only seven days.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a specific case and links it to a particular תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a shaving in the middle of the term, which would cost thirty days of regrowth.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about a shaving after the term, where רבי אליעזר says only seven days are at stake.

steps.title: Why does רבי אליעזר say seven days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אליעזר's seven-day rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask where רבי אליעזר gets the number seven. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer to the challenge depends on רבי אליעזר's rule, so the גמרא wants to know what it is based on. This is a request for the source, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule used in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that after completion only seven days are lost.

steps.title: Learning the shaving of purity from the shaving of impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר compares the shaving at the end of a pure term to the shaving after טומאה. Just as the טומאה case involves seven days, so does the purity case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns the shaving of purity from the shaving of impurity. Just as the shaving of impurity is seven days, so too the shaving of purity is seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אליעזר's source. He compares the two kinds of shaving a נזיר does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר who became טמא waits seven days to become pure and then shaves. רבי אליעזר applies the same seven to the regular end-of-term shaving. So if he is shaved after his term is finished, only seven days are at stake.

keyTerms.meaning: learns, derives
the shaving of purity (at the end of a regular term)
the shaving of impurity (after becoming טמא)
just as… so too… (a comparison)

phrases.english: He derives the shaving of purity
from the shaving of impurity.
Just as the shaving of impurity involves seven days,
so too the shaving of purity involves seven days.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A comparison: the shaving of purity is like the shaving of impurity, which involves seven days.

steps.title: Hair grows a bend-to-root length in seven days
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים know that hair grows enough to bend its tip to its root in seven days. So the hair left on the נזיר already covers the seven days at stake.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים have a tradition that in every seven days, hair grows enough to bend its tip to its root.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to the challenge from step 2 with a known fact about how fast hair grows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the term is finished, only seven days of growth are needed (step 3). The hair the bandits left, enough to bend tip to root, equals seven days of growth. So nothing is missing and he loses nothing, even if hair grows from the bottom.

keyTerms.meaning: they know for certain / they have a tradition
hair
grows, comes

steps.whatToRemember: Hair grows from the bottom. The ברייתא of the נזיר shaved by bandits fits this, because it is about a shaving after his term. רבי אליעזר says only seven days are at stake then, and hair grows a bend-to-root length in seven days.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא saves a ברייתא by combining a narrow case, a specific תנא's rule and a known fact about nature. The conclusion that hair grows from the bottom stays standing.

phrases.english: And the חכמים have an accepted tradition
that in every seven days hair grows
enough to bend its tip to its root.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the challenge of step 2 and finishes the answer begun in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a fact about nature that completes the answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even after completion, the lost hair would make him lose days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The remaining bend-to-root hair equals seven days of growth, so he loses nothing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא fits the view that hair grows from the bottom.

steps.title: The משנה: any way of removing hair makes the נזיר liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a נזיר who shaves with a razor or with scissors, or pulls out even a tiny bit of hair, is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נזיר who shaved, whether with a razor or with scissors, or who pulled out any amount of hair, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. Next, it will look for the source of this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not limit the איסור to a razor. Scissors count, and even pulling out a few hairs counts. This is a wide rule, so the גמרא will need to show where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A razor
Scissors (literally 'a pair', meaning two blades)
Pulled out a few hairs, a little at a time
Liable, meaning he gets punished

phrases.english: A nazir who shaved
whether with a razor or with scissors,
or who pulled out any amount, is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָזִיר שֶׁגִּילַּח בֵּין בְּתַעַר בֵּין בְּזוּג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of a נזיר shaved by bandits and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר is liable for removing hair with a razor, with scissors, or by pulling out even a small amount.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה learns the other methods from 'He shall be holy'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the word 'razor' alone would only cover a razor. רבי יאשיה learns from 'קדוש יהיה גדל פרע' that tearing, plucking and pulling out are also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Razor' teaches me only a razor. How do I know he is liable if he tore out, plucked, or pulled out any amount? The פסוק says: 'He shall be holy, he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.' These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the source for the משנה's wide rule. According to רבי יאשיה, the source is the phrase about growing his hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'a razor shall not pass over his head' only mention a razor. רבי יאשיה reads 'let the hair grow' as a command to keep all his hair. So any way of removing hair breaks that command.

keyTerms.meaning: I only have, meaning this word alone teaches only this case
Tore out (hair)
Plucked out (hair)
From where do we know?
The פסוק says, introducing the source
Let the locks grow long

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught:
"Razor": I have only a razor.
phrases.notes: This is from the פסוק 'a razor shall not pass over his head' (במדבר 6:5).

phrases.aramaic: תָּלַשׁ, מֵירַט, סִיפְסֵף כׇּל שֶׁהוּא, מִנַּיִן
phrases.english: If he tore out, plucked, or pulled out any amount, from where do we know?
The verse says:
"He shall be holy, he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow,"

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״תַּעַר״, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא תַּעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the משנה's rule that non-razor methods also make him liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יאשיה, 'קדוש יהיה גדל פרע' makes all methods of removing hair forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: only a razor makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן disagrees: the word 'razor' teaches only a razor, so plucking or pulling out hair does not make him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: 'Razor' teaches me only a razor. If he plucked, tore out, or pulled out any amount, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives the opposite view. For him, the punishment applies only to a razor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן reads the פסוק narrowly and stops at the word 'razor'. He does not accept רבי יאשיה's extra source. This sets up the question the גמרא asks next.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount, even a tiny bit
Exempt, meaning not punished

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan says:
"Razor": I have only a razor.

phrases.aramaic: מֵירַט, תָּלַשׁ, סִיפְסֵף כׇּל שֶׁהוּא — פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: If he plucked, tore out, or pulled out any amount, he is exempt.

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here means he is not punished for plucking. The גמרא does not discuss here whether plucking is allowed.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבי יאשיה from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יונתן, only shaving with a razor brings punishment. Plucking or pulling out hair does not.

steps.title: Challenge: what about 'He shall be holy'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבי יונתן: the פסוק says 'קדוש יהיה', so what does he do with it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'He shall be holy'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יונתן. If he limits the איסור to a razor, the phrase רבי יאשיה used seems to have no job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every phrase in the תורה must teach something. For רבי יאשיה, 'קדוש יהיה' adds the other methods. רבי יונתן has to explain what this phrase teaches according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (used to open a challenge from a פסוק)
He shall be holy

phrases.english: But isn't it written: "He shall be holy"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יונתן in step 9 using the פסוק רבי יאשיה cited in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונתן's view that only a razor brings liability
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'קדוש יהיה גדל פרע' seems to forbid every way of removing hair. If it does not, what does it teach?

steps.title: A razor breaks both a positive מצוה and a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יונתן, 'קדוש יהיה' teaches that shaving with a razor breaks both a positive מצוה‎ (עשה) and a prohibition (לא תעשה).
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase comes to say that if he shaved with a razor, he breaks both a positive מצוה and a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יונתן. The phrase does not add new methods. It adds a second מצוה to the razor case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה uses 'קדוש יהיה' to make the איסור wider and cover more methods. רבי יונתן uses it to make the razor case heavier, because it now breaks an עשה too. So the phrase still teaches something.

keyTerms.meaning: That is to say, it comes to teach
A positive מצוה (something you must do)
A prohibition (something you must not do)

phrases.english: That comes to say that if he shaved it with a razor
he stands in violation of a positive מצוה and a prohibition.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יאשיה: 'קדוש יהיה' adds more methods, so all are forbidden. רבי יונתן: only a razor is punished, and 'קדוש יהיה' adds an עשה on top of the לא תעשה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the phrase a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'קדוש יהיה' must forbid all methods of hair removal.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יונתן, 'קדוש יהיה' adds an עשה to razor shaving and does not add new methods.

steps.title: Another ברייתא learns all methods from 'shall not pass over his head'
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא learns that tearing, plucking and pulling out are forbidden from the words 'לא יעבור על ראשו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: 'Razor' teaches me only a razor. How do I know he is liable if he tore out, plucked, or pulled out any amount? The פסוק says: 'shall not pass over his head.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא with a second source for the wide rule. This time the source is the rest of the razor פסוק itself, 'לא יעבור על ראשו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the words 'shall not pass over his head' are read by themselves to mean nothing may remove his hair. That covers every method, not only a razor. This leads straight to the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall not pass over his head

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:
"Razor": I have only a razor.

phrases.aramaic: תָּלַשׁ, מֵירַט, סִיפְסֵף כׇּל שֶׁהוּא, מִנַּיִן
phrases.english: If he tore out, plucked, or pulled out any amount, from where do we know?
The verse says: "shall not pass over his head."
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק, read to mean that nothing at all may remove his hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the rule from step 7, besides רבי יאשיה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לא יעבור על ראשו' forbids every method of removing hair.

steps.title: If everything is included, why say 'razor'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: since we include every method anyway, why does the פסוק mention a razor at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since in the end we include everything, why does the פסוק say 'A razor shall not pass over his head'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading. If every method is forbidden, the word 'razor' seems unneeded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used 'shall not pass over his head' to cover everything. That makes the word 'razor' look extra. So the word must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end we will include
What does the פסוק come to teach?

phrases.english: And since we end up including everything,
what does the verse come to teach by saying
"A razor shall not pass over his head"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁסּוֹפֵינוּ לְרַבּוֹת כֹּל דָּבָר, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the extra word left over after step 12's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word 'razor' teach, if all methods are forbidden anyway?

steps.title: 'Razor' teaches that the final shaving must use a razor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that 'razor' teaches that the final shaving at the end of a pure נזירות must be done with a razor. This cannot be learned from a מצורע, and the reason continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we have not learned that the final shaving must be done with a razor. To learn it from a מצורע is impossible,
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins its answer: the word 'razor' tells us which tool to use for the final shaving. It then starts explaining why we cannot learn this from a מצורע, and that explanation continues in the next text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the final shaving does not say which tool to use. A מצורע must shave with a razor, but the ברייתא says we cannot copy that rule over to a נזיר. So the extra word 'razor' is needed here.

keyTerms.meaning: The final shaving, done when a נזיר finishes his term in purity
A person with צרעת, who must shave as part of his purification
It is impossible

phrases.english: Because we have not learned regarding the final shaving

phrases.english: that it must be with a razor.

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'razor' is not taken away from the איסור. It gets an added job: telling us how the final shaving is done.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13, and begins a side discussion about the מצורע.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Razor' teaches that the final shaving must be done with a razor. We cannot learn this from a מצורע, and the reason continues in the next text.
